stem: Arrange the compounds in increasing acidity of their $\alpha$-hydrogens: ethyl acetate, cyclohexanone, propanal and cyclohexane-1,3-dione.

verdicts.working: Approximate α-H pKa values: ethyl acetate 25, cyclohexanone 20, propanal 17, and cyclohexane-1,3-dione 5. Lower pKa means greater acidity, giving option C.

working:
Conjugate-base stability: ester enolate < ketone enolate < aldehyde enolate < 1,3-dicarbonyl enolate.
Thus acidity increases: ethyl acetate < cyclohexanone < propanal < cyclohexane-1,3-dione.

Independent check: Approximate α-H pKa values: ethyl acetate 25, cyclohexanone 20, propanal 17, and cyclohexane-1,3-dione 5. Lower pKa means greater acidity, giving option C.
solution:
Greater stabilization of the conjugate base increases the acidity of the $lpha$-hydrogens. Enolate stability increases from ester to ketone to aldehyde, while the 1,3-dione enolate is additionally stabilized by resonance with both carbonyl groups.
$$\text{Ethyl acetate} < \text{cyclohexanone} < \text{propanal} < \text{cyclohexane-1,3-dione}$$
